purpose: Declared model routing. Task class -> tier, agent template -> task class, observed session -> task class. Read by bin/heimdall-tier (declaration + conformance) and bin/lib/tier_audit.py (drift audit). Changing a tier here changes what the audit calls drift, so this file is the single place the routing decision lives.
no_pinned_ids: Tiers are BARE ALIASES on purpose. Claude Code resolves opus|sonnet|haiku to the current generation of that tier; a pinned full model id in an operational path silently ages (that is how Opus 5 shipped while Heimdall kept spawning claude-opus-4-8). Pin only for bench/eval reproducibility, via HEIMDALL_MODEL_<TIER>. model_id_tier_patterns below classify OBSERVED history and are therefore version-free regexes, not pins.
rank_note: fable shares opus's rank because spec 2.1 writes the top row as 'Opus / Fable' — either satisfies that class, so an opus-class task seen on fable is not tier drift. Fable's extra cost is governed by the ZDR policy gate and the weekly allowance, not by the drift rank.

cache_price_multipliers.note: Every cache line is a fixed multiple of the tier's own input price, identical across haiku/sonnet/opus/fable. This is why the counterfactual cost of a request at another tier is a single scalar on the forensics harness's cost(), not a second price model that could disagree with it.

non_zdr_note: Claude Fable 5 requires 30-day data retention; a zero-data-retention org gets 400 invalid_request_error on every Fable request. Selection is therefore deny-by-default and must fail LOUDLY — a silent downgrade to a cheaper tier would hide the fact that a repo cannot run this tier at all.

hook.summary: Hook bodies: fires per event, bounded input, decision is a classification not a design.

classifier.summary: Label a bounded input against a fixed set of categories.

formatter.summary: Lint, format, rename, mechanical rewrite with a deterministic oracle.

janitor.summary: Janitor and reaper tasks: sweep stale state, close orphans, prune logs.

marker_check.summary: Presence/absence checks for markers, sentinels and required fields.

coder.summary: Standard coder agents: implement to a stated scope with tests.

test_writer.summary: Write and run tests against an existing implementation.

doc.summary: Documentation agents: write and sync prose against shipped behaviour.

triage.summary: Triage: read signals, group them, decide what deserves escalation.

orchestrator.summary: Decompose work, spawn and supervise agents, hold the plan.
orchestrator.no_downgrade_reason: The orchestrator decides which gates run at all. Weakening it weakens every gate downstream of it.

architecture.summary: Architecture and design reasoning; decisions that outlive the session.

security_critical.summary: Security-critical reasoning: threat modelling, vulnerability assessment, dependency and secret audit.
security_critical.no_downgrade_reason: A cheaper check that misses a vulnerability costs far more than the whole $57.73 this table was built to recover. If the spend is unacceptable, reduce FREQUENCY — never the tier.

gate_adjudication.summary: Adjudicating a gate: review, verification, deciding whether evidence actually proves the claim.
gate_adjudication.no_downgrade_reason: A gate that passes work it should have failed is worse than no gate, because it manufactures false confidence.

forensics.summary: Incident and spend forensics: reconstruct what happened from evidence.
